name: Slack
verdict: You can have other workspaces installing an unlisted app within an hour, but a paid or commercial AI agent needs Slack Marketplace approval. Without it, Slack's terms don't allow commercial distribution and conversations.history/replies are capped at 1 request/min with 15 messages. Start getting 10 active installs now (Slack's minimum again since July 2026, and you must stay at 10+ for the whole review) and budget 1-3 months for review.

difficulty.label: Hard
difficulty.rationale: Turning on unlisted distribution takes one click and has no review. However, Slack's API Terms forbid commercially distributing an app (including a free app tied to a paid product) without authorization, which normally means a Marketplace listing. Since 29 May 2025, newly created unlisted commercial apps and new installs also get a crippling 1 req/min, 15-object limit on conversations.history/replies. Marketplace review requires a minimum number of active installs, a preliminary review of up to 10 business days, and a functional review of up to 10 weeks.

first_token.note: Create the app at api.slack.com/apps, add bot scopes, then click Install to Workspace in your own workspace. You get an xoxb- bot token right away, with no review.

production.active_effort: 3-7 days (landing page, privacy policy, support page, demo video, scope justifications, test account, AI disclosures)
production.waiting: Time to reach the minimum active-workspace installs, plus up to 10 business days of preliminary review and up to 10 weeks of functional review
production.note: Three things drive the wait: (1) collecting the required active-workspace installs while you're throttled as an unlisted app, (2) the functional review queue, (3) resubmissions. A resubmission during preliminary review resets your place in the queue. Enhanced-review scopes such as *:history and files:read make the review longer.

cost: Free. There is no fee for API access, unlisted distribution or a Marketplace listing. Agent/assistant features need a paid Slack plan on the customer side.

paths.name: Internal app (single workspace / your own org)
paths.who_for: Testing, or a customer building the agent for its own workspace
paths.limits: Full Tier 3 limits on conversations.history/replies (50+ req/min, up to 1,000 objects). Only installable in the workspace that owns the app.

paths.name: Unlisted public distribution (Manage Distribution)
paths.who_for: Pilots with early customers, dev/test installs in other workspaces
paths.limits: conversations.history and conversations.replies are capped at Tier 1 (1 req/min, max 15 objects per call) for apps created and installs made since 29 May 2025 (Slack's changelog says installs that pre-date that are not impacted; third-party claims of a 3 March 2026 cutover for existing installs are unconfirmed). Slack terms forbid commercial distribution without authorization. Workspaces may block non-Marketplace apps or require admin approval.

paths.name: Slack Marketplace listing
paths.who_for: Any commercially distributed agent (paid, freemium, or free but tied to a paid product)
paths.review: Preliminary review (up to 10 business days), then functional review (up to 10 weeks for new apps, 6 weeks for updates)
paths.limits: Standard rate limits. Requires a minimum number of active installs (10 active workspaces since July 2026, maintained throughout review) before you can submit. Every later scope or feature change needs re-review. AI agent/assistant apps must not store Slack data (zero-copy).

prerequisites.item: A Slack workspace where you can install apps (a free dev workspace works; a Developer Program sandbox is recommended)
prerequisites.note: Use it as your development workspace. Marketplace testing must happen in a different workspace.

prerequisites.item: A public HTTPS backend with an OAuth redirect endpoint (plus Events/Interactivity request URLs if used)
prerequisites.note: Slack requires SSL for redirect, interactivity, options-load and Events API URLs.

prerequisites.item: Secure token store (DB/secret manager) for bot tokens, user tokens, and rotating refresh tokens
prerequisites.note: With token rotation, refresh tokens are single-use. Always persist the newest one.

prerequisites.item: For Marketplace: a public landing page, privacy policy, support contact (2-business-day response), and test credentials for your service
prerequisites.note: The landing page must be a dedicated, login-free web page, not a PDF or a repo.

prerequisites.item: For Marketplace: installs in at least 10 active workspaces (used in the last 28 days, sandboxes excluded)
prerequisites.note: Submissions below the threshold are blocked automatically, and the app must stay at 10+ during the entire review (Slack changelog 2026-09-01).

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps > Create New App > 'From a manifest' (recommended so config lives in git) or 'From scratch'. Choose the development workspace. App name and icon appear on the consent screen.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs and scopes
steps.detail: Open OAuth & Permissions. Under Redirect URLs, add your https callback(s); no '#' fragments are allowed. Under Scopes, add Bot Token Scopes (e.g. chat:write, app_mentions:read, channels:history, im:history). Add User Token Scopes only if the agent must act as the user (e.g. search:read). In the authorize URL, bot scopes go in `scope` and user scopes in `user_scope`.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation (one-way)
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions > Advanced token security via token rotation > Opt in (manifest: settings.token_rotation_enabled: true). Access tokens then expire every 12 hours (expires_in 43200) with an xoxe. prefix. Refresh via POST oauth.v2.access with grant_type=refresh_token. You can't turn this off once it's on, so build the refresh logic first.

steps.title: Enable Events / Agents & AI Apps features as needed
steps.detail: Event Subscriptions: set the Request URL and subscribe to bot events (app_mention, message.im, etc.). If you use the assistant/agent surface, enable it in the app config. Verify requests with the Signing Secret; verification tokens are deprecated. Prefer Events over polling history, because the history methods are heavily throttled for unlisted apps.

steps.title: Install to your own workspace and get a token
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions > Install to Workspace (or run your own /slack/install route). Bot token (xoxb-) is top-level in the oauth.v2.access response; user token is under authed_user. Check the `state` param on callback.

steps.title: (Optional) Opt in to org-wide deployment for Enterprise orgs
steps.detail: Add at least one bot scope, then open Org Level Apps in the sidebar > Opt-In > Yes, Opt-in (manifest: org_deploy_enabled: true). An Enterprise org admin/owner must install at the org level. The oauth.v2.access response then has is_enterprise_install: true, team: null, and enterprise.id. The admin must add the app to workspaces afterwards, so redirect them to do that.

steps.title: Activate unlisted public distribution
steps.detail: Basic Information > Manage Distribution > 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces'. Complete the checklist, then click Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL. There is no review, but remember the commercial-distribution and rate-limit restrictions.

steps.title: Collect the required active installs
steps.detail: Get the app used in at least 10 non-sandbox workspaces that are active within 28 days, and keep it there through review (Slack changelog 2026-09-01). Design pilot features around the Events API (message events) and RTS/search rather than bulk history reads.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace materials
steps.detail: Prepare a landing page (overview, how it works, install path, next steps, privacy link), a privacy policy (data collected, use, retention, access/deletion requests, contact), and a support page. Write a justification for every scope (only for features you can demo). Prepare a test account with dummy data plus third-party credentials, and a demo video covering install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall. For AI apps, add the Security & Compliance answers (model used, retention, LLM data tenancy/residency) and an inaccurate-output disclaimer.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Open Manage Distribution > Submit to Slack Marketplace and complete the submission form. Reviewers can't access your workspaces, so give them an install method plus credentials for your service.
steps.wait: Preliminary up to 10 business days; functional up to 10 weeks

steps.title: Publish and manage changes
steps.detail: After approval, scope and config changes go through Published App Settings and need re-review (up to 6 weeks for published apps). Token rotation for listed apps is set under Published App Settings.
steps.wait: Re-review up to 6 weeks per change

review.trigger: Any commercial distribution: users could pay for your product, including freemium apps and free apps tied to a paid product. Slack's API Terms require authorization, which in practice means a Marketplace listing. You also need it to escape the Tier 1 history/replies limit. Internal apps and non-commercial unlisted apps need no review.
review.process: Meet the active-install minimum, then submit. Preliminary review checks the listing, docs, scope justifications and installability. Functional review means a reviewer tests the features and scopes. Slack may run an advanced security review at any time. It is a moment-in-time review, not a code review.
review.typical_wait: Official maximums are 10 business days (preliminary) plus 10 weeks (functional, new apps). Community reports range from 2 weeks (an expedited, viral AI agent) to 2-3 months typical.
reviewers_check: Each scope maps to a working, demoable feature, with minimal scopes and no bot/user duplication
Landing page, privacy policy and support meet guidelines
Install, onboarding, use and uninstall work in a non-dev workspace
Security: tokens stored securely, `state` used, TLS 1.2+, requests verified with signing secret
AI disclosures: model, retention, data tenancy/residency, no training on Slack data, disclaimer about inaccurate output
Agent/assistant apps don't store Slack data (zero-copy) and disclose that a paid Slack plan is needed
common_rejections: Requesting scopes for features not yet built, or broad/legacy/restricted scopes (admin.*, identity.*, search:read)
Missing or non-working test credentials, or giving Slack workspace credentials instead of an install method
Bugs, poor UX, app not production-ready or still in beta

pre_approval_limits: Unlisted commercially distributed apps: conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request/min with max and default limit=15 objects (apps created / installs made since 2025-05-29; Slack says older existing installs are not impacted)
Slack API Terms: no commercial distribution without authorization (Marketplace or separate agreement)
Workspaces with 'Approve apps' turned on make members request the app, and an admin must approve it
Some workspaces allow only Marketplace-listed apps

oauth.refresh_tokens: Only with token rotation, which is opt-in and irreversible. Refresh tokens are single-use, each refresh returns a new one, and at most 2 active access tokens are allowed per 12h window. PKCE-enabled (public client) apps get refresh tokens that expire after 30 days.
oauth.access_token_lifetime: No expiry by default; tokens last until revoked or the app is uninstalled. With rotation, 12 hours (xoxe. prefix).
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: HTTPS required. redirect_uri must match, or be a subdirectory of, a Redirect URL configured on OAuth & Permissions. You can register multiple URLs. Use the same redirect_uri in the authorize and token steps, otherwise you get bad_redirect_uri. No '#' fragments. Localhost and custom schemes only with PKCE (GA 2026-03-30), and those can't request bot scopes.
oauth.scopes: Granular scopes, split into bot scopes (`scope`) and user scopes (`user_scope`). *:history, files:read, search:read.*, canvases:read and admin.* trigger enhanced Marketplace review. admin.* is generally limited to partners. Unused or duplicate scopes get rejected.
oauth.tenant_notes: Each workspace install yields its own token keyed by team.id. Enterprise orgs: opt in to Org Level Apps and an org admin installs once (is_enterprise_install=true, enterprise.id), then adds the app to workspaces. Workspace or org admins may require app approval. Rate limits are per app per workspace per method.

gotchas.title: Unlisted AI agents get only 15 messages per minute of history
gotchas.detail: Since 2025-05-29, for apps created or installed after that date, commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps can call conversations.history/replies only once per minute, with 15 objects max. Internal apps and Marketplace apps aren't affected. Agents degrade silently, getting less context with no error. Workarounds: build context from Events API message events, use the Real-time Search API, or get listed.

gotchas.title: Commercial distribution needs Slack's authorization
gotchas.detail: The API Terms (effective 2025-10-10) forbid commercially distributing an app unless authorized. The definition covers paid, freemium, and free apps connected to a paid product. For most apps, authorization means a Marketplace listing.

gotchas.title: Don't train LLMs on Slack data, and don't build persistent indexes
gotchas.detail: API Terms: you may not use API Data to train a large language model, or bulk export message/file data. With the Data Access/RTS APIs you can't create persistent copies, archives or indexes of other orgs' data. Marketplace guidelines also say agent/assistant apps must not store Slack data (zero-copy). This rules out the usual RAG-index-everything design.

gotchas.title: Marketplace submission needs real installs first
gotchas.detail: Submissions are auto-blocked below the active-workspace threshold (workspaces active in the last 28 days, sandboxes excluded). The 2025-07-08 changelog lowered it to 5, but current review docs still say 10. Plan your pilot program accordingly.

gotchas.title: Token rotation can't be undone
gotchas.detail: Once you opt in, every token expires in 12h and refresh tokens are single-use. If you lose the latest refresh token (race between workers, failed DB write), the user has to reinstall. Make the refresh-and-persist step atomic or locked.

gotchas.title: Review is long and changes are re-reviewed
gotchas.detail: Functional review can take up to 10 weeks (6 weeks for updates). Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue position. After listing, adding a scope means another review.

gotchas.title: Admin approval and Marketplace-only workspaces
gotchas.detail: Workspaces can require admin approval, or allow only Marketplace apps. Users then see a 'Request' flow and the install stalls until an admin acts. Fewer and narrower scopes get approved faster.

gotchas.title: Enterprise org installs return no team
gotchas.detail: An org-wide install returns team: null and is_enterprise_install: true. Code that keys tokens by team.id breaks. Store by enterprise.id and send the admin to add the app to workspaces.

gotchas.title: Enhanced-review scopes
gotchas.detail: *:history, files:read, search:read.* and canvases:read are exactly what agents want, and they trigger deeper review. search:read (user) is listed as generally unsuitable. Justify each one with a demoable feature.

blockers.cause: redirect_uri isn't a configured Redirect URL (or a subdirectory of one), or differs between the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls
blockers.fix: Add the exact https URL under OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs and pass the identical value in both steps.

blockers.symptom: Agent sees only ~15 recent messages / ratelimited on conversations.history
blockers.fix: Use Events API to capture messages as they happen, use Real-time Search API, or get a Marketplace listing. Internal apps aren't affected.

blockers.cause: Fewer active-workspace installs than the threshold
blockers.fix: Grow pilot installs (non-sandbox, active in the last 28 days) to the threshold.

blockers.cause: Reused an old single-use refresh token, or lost the newest one
blockers.fix: Always persist the refresh_token from each response before using the access token. Serialize refreshes per installation. As a last resort, reinstall.

blockers.symptom: User clicks Add to Slack but sees 'Request to install'
blockers.fix: The workspace admin approves under app management. Give customers an admin-facing scope explanation.

agent_can: generate app manifest (scopes, redirect URLs, events, org_deploy_enabled, token_rotation_enabled)
implement OAuth callback with state check and token storage
design Events-API-based context capture to avoid history rate limits
draft privacy policy, landing page and support page
write demo video script and test plan
human_must: sign in to Slack / own the dev workspace
accept Slack API Terms and the Marketplace agreement
click Activate Public Distribution and Submit
recruit pilot workspaces to reach the install threshold

evidence.note: Effective May 29, 2025 for new apps and new installs

evidence.note: Official page: "These rate limits will not impact existing installations." 3 Mar 2026 date appears only in third-party posts (allanninal.dev, dev.to).

Token rotation: 12h expiry, single-use refresh tokens, irreversible, xoxe. prefix
evidence.note: "Token rotation may not be turned off once it's turned on."

evidence.note: Unlisted distribution described as suited to pilots

evidence.note: Requires at least one bot scope before opt-in

Third-party summary of 2026 Slack review stages and timelines; 5-workspace prerequisite

evidence.claim: As of July 2026 Marketplace submissions need at least 10 active-workspace installs, maintained for the entire review (temporary lower threshold ended)
evidence.note: "at least 10 installations on active workspaces"; also stated in Marketplace review guide

uncertain: Whether the conversations.history/replies 1 req/min limit now also applies to installs made before 29 May 2025: Slack's official changelog says existing installs are not impacted, but several third-party posts claim enforcement on existing installs by 3 March 2026. Assume the limit applies to anything you ship now.
Exact items in the Manage Distribution checklist (e.g. 'Remove hard-coded information') weren't listed in the docs page fetched.
Whether Real-Time Search API access requires a Marketplace listing, and its rate limits for unlisted apps, weren't confirmed.
Real-world functional review duration varies widely (2 weeks to ~3 months). The data points are community-reported.
Whether the API Terms' LLM clause restricts inference-time use beyond training. The terms only explicitly ban training, plus general minimization and no-persistent-index rules.

probes.what: Authorize endpoint with fake client_id while signed out
probes.result: Redirects to 'Find your workspace' sign-in; Slack resolves the workspace before validating client_id
probes.method: Live browser request (no account created, no credentials used)
